content: Stimulant laxatives are prescribed to treat constipation, to prepare the bowel for rectal or bowel examinations, or prior to surgery. They function by increasing bowel movements and are also used to manage certain intestinal conditions. In some cases, they may be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Stimulant laxatives are available in various forms, including liquids, powders, granules, tablets, and suppositories. Follow the instructions on the package or prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take stimulant laxatives exactly as directed. Do not take more or less than prescribed, and do not take them more frequently than instructed by your doctor. Take stimulant laxatives on an empty stomach with a full 8-ounce glass of water. If taken with food, the effects may be delayed. Most stimulant laxatives are taken at bedtime, with results typically occurring by morning; however, some products may take up to 24 hours to produce a bowel movement. Castor oil works faster than other laxatives and should not be taken at bedtime. To mask the unpleasant taste of castor oil, refrigerate it and mix it with cold orange juice just before drinking. Castor oil should not be used routinely to treat constipation. Do not crush or chew bisacodyl tablets, and avoid taking them within one hour of consuming milk or antacids. If using a suppository, follow these steps: Remove the wrapper. Moisten the tip of the suppository with lukewarm water. Lie on your left side and raise your right knee to your chest. (If you are left-handed, lie on your right side and raise your left knee.) Using your finger, insert the suppository high into the rectum. Hold it in place for a few moments and try to retain it for as long as possible. Wash your hands thoroughly after use. Do not use stimulant laxatives for longer than one week unless directed by your doctor. Avoid exceeding the recommended dose, as overuse can lead to serious side effects. If you do not have a bowel movement after taking a stimulant laxative, contact your doctor. Prolonged use of stimulant laxatives may result in dependence, and overuse can cause permanent damage to the intestines and colon. If your symptoms do not improve while using a stimulant laxative, consult your doctor. Do not give stimulant laxatives to children under 10 years old unless instructed by a doctor. Before taking stimulant laxatives, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to any medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially antacids, antibiotics, pain or seizure medications, medications for depression, heart disease, or blood pressure, and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have or have ever had diabetes, heart disease, high blood pressure, or intestinal disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking stimulant laxatives, contact your doctor. Maintain a regular diet and exercise routine to support normal bowel function. Consume a high-fiber diet and drink plenty of fluids (six to eight glasses daily). Avoid foods that contribute to constipation, such as processed cheese. If you are on a low-sugar, low-calorie, or low-sodium diet, consult your doctor or pharmacist before taking a stimulant laxative. If you miss a scheduled dose of stimulant laxatives, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for the missed one. Stimulant laxatives may cause side effects. Cascara and senna can cause yellow-brown urine, which is harmless. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: Diarrhea Upset stomach Vomiting Irritation Stomach cramping If you experience any of the following severe side effects, stop taking stimulant laxatives and contact your doctor immediately: Bloody stools Severe cramping Pain Weakness Dizziness Unusual tiredness Rectal bleeding If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. If you have any questions about taking this medication, ask your pharmacist for clarification.
